item.author: Fran Lu
item.dc:creator: Fran Lu
item.description: Chinese people use the phrase “yao chan wan guan,” or “carrying ten thousand strings of cash around the waist,” to describe wealth. But how much was a string of cash, and what could one buy in ancient China? Guan was a traditional Chinese unit of account. Literally referring to the string used to thread coins together, it emerged alongside the round coin with a square hole, which first appeared during the Qin dynasty (221–206 BC). A guan generally equalled a string of 1,000 individual copper or...
item.title: What’s the true worth behind Chinese phrase ‘carrying 10,000 strings of cash around the waist’
